title: Payslips & tax (country overlay)
examples: How do I know if the tax taken out is correct?
What are the main types of deductions I should look for?
Can you explain the difference between gross and net pay again?

explain.say: Today we are learning to read your payslip carefully. This document shows how much you earn and what is taken out.

draw.text: Gross vs Net Pay: Understanding Your Payslip

explain.say: Gross pay is your total earnings before anything is taken out. This is the full amount you earned before deductions.

draw.text: Gross Pay: Total Earnings Before Deductions

explain.say: Deductions are amounts taken away from your gross pay. These often include tax and pension contributions.
Net pay is the money you actually take home. It is what remains after all the deductions are subtracted.
For example, if your gross pay is three thousand dollars. And your deductions total five hundred dollars. Your net pay is eighteen hundred dollars.
In real life, your bank transfer shows your net pay. This is the money available for your rent and bills. Always check this amount.

faq.q: What is the difference between gross and net pay?
faq.a: Gross pay is your total earnings before any money is taken out. Net pay is the final amount you receive after all deductions are made.
asks: Why is my pay less than my gross pay?

faq.q: What are common deductions I should look out for?
faq.a: Common deductions include income tax, national insurance, and pension contributions. These help fund public services and your retirement.
asks: What gets taken out of my salary?

faq.q: Does the tax rate change every pay period?
faq.a: Tax rates are generally based on your annual income and tax code. Your employer adjusts this based on your tax year.
asks: Will my tax deduction change next month?

faq.q: If I change jobs, will my deductions change?
faq.a: Yes, your deductions can change because your new salary and tax situation might be different. Always check the new payslip.
asks: Do I need to update my tax information?
How does a new job affect my deductions?

faq.q: What is the purpose of pension deductions?
faq.a: Pension deductions save money for your retirement years. This money is invested to provide you with income when you stop working.
asks: Why do I have to pay into a pension?

facts: Gross pay represents the total wages earned before any subtractions.
Net pay is the actual amount of money deposited into your bank account.
Deductions cover mandatory items like income tax and voluntary items like pension contributions.
The payslip is a legal document detailing your pay period earnings.

quiz.say: If your gross pay is five hundred pounds and your deductions are one hundred pounds, what is your net pay?
quiz.why: Net pay is always calculated by subtracting the total deductions from the gross pay.

wrong.1: This is adding the amounts together, which is incorrect for finding the remaining balance.
wrong.2: This forgets to subtract the deductions entirely from the total pay.
wrong.3: This assumes that all your pay is taken away by the deductions.

quiz.say: Which term describes the total amount earned before deductions are taken out?
quiz.why: Gross pay is the starting figure before any deductions are subtracted from it.

wrong.0: Net pay is the final amount received, not the starting total.
wrong.1: This is another term for net pay, which is the result, not the starting amount.
wrong.2: Deductions are the amounts that are taken out, not the total amount earned.

quiz.say: If a payslip shows a tax deduction of a fixed amount, this deduction is an example of:
quiz.why: Tax is a mandatory deduction that must be taken out by law from your earnings.

wrong.0: Gross pay is the total amount before any deductions are made.
wrong.1: Net pay is the final amount after all deductions are calculated.
wrong.2: Income is a general term for earnings, not the specific category on the payslip.
